name: TI_Delay
summary: Suspends the task for a number of game-clock milliseconds (or seconds + ms).
semantics: Suspends the calling task. delay = arg1 if argc!=2, or arg1*1000+arg2 if argc==2 (units: game-clock milliseconds, the clock is EngineConfig+0x718, the same as TI_GetAbsTime). A timer node is queued with due = clock + delay + jitter, jitter = rand()*min(delay/16+1, 256)/0x8000 for delay<0x1000 (i.e. 0..delay/16), else 0..255 (so the wait is slightly LONGER than requested, never shorter); negative delay gives jitter 0 (delay/16+1 <= 0 -> 0) and fires on the next tick. TiTick (every frame, before script run) fires every node with (due - clock) <= 0, resuming the task with int 0. The task wakes on a LATER frame (not the same frame). A killed task id is ignored when the timer fires.
x3_src: differs: random numbers come from per-task RNG channels (x3::rng, docs/arch/rng_split_r2.md), not the shared CRT rand(); same distribution, different sequence; not in bugs.md
notes: TiDispatch 0x004b1300; TiScheduleDelay 0x004b0b00; TiTick 0x004b0e00. Dispatcher returns 1 without calling ResumeTask (the task waits). Fires also when time warp advances the clock.

name: TI_DelayRandom
summary: Suspends the task for base + random(range) game-clock milliseconds.
semantics: Like TI_Delay with delay = arg1 + (arg2>0 ? RandScaled(arg2) = rand()*arg2/0x8000 : 0), i.e. arg1 + [0, arg2-1] (arg2<=0 => delay=arg1). Always the two-argument (base,range) form; arg2 is NOT seconds. Plus the TiScheduleDelay jitter. Wakes with int 0.
x3_src: differs: random numbers come from per-task RNG channels (x3::rng, docs/arch/rng_split_r2.md), not the shared CRT rand(); same distribution, different sequence; not in bugs.md

name: TI_GetAbsTime
summary: Returns the game clock in milliseconds (time-warped).
semantics: Result = EngineConfig+0x718 = the game clock (ms, scaled by time warp; set by TI_SetAbsTime, advanced each frame). Sync.

name: TI_CmpTime
semantics: Result = t1 - t2 as a plain 32-bit wrapping subtraction (arg1 - arg2). No clock access. Sync.

name: TI_WaitForStart
summary: Suspends the task until the next frame tick (yield one frame).
semantics: TiEnqueueImmediate(ctx, task id) (AP 0x004b0aa0): appends a node to the immediate list; the task waits (state 2, pc saved in a savegame). The next Script::TiTick (once per main-loop frame, after the clock update) completes every immediate node through the group completion callback with int 0 (remaining time is 0 for non-interrupt completions), so the task resumes on the next frame. The immediate pass is skipped while the queue flag ImmediatePaused (bit 0) is set; no code sets it in practice. If no node can be allocated the completion is called at once (the task resumes immediately with 0). Arguments ignored. A killed task id is ignored at completion. Script::TiDispatch AP 0x004b1300, FL 0x004cdf50 (same case layout).

name: TI_WaitForInterrupt
summary: Suspends the task until a timeout or a TI_Interrupt with the same key (returns the remaining ms on interrupt).
semantics: Suspends the calling task until either the timeout expires or TI_Interrupt(key) is called with the same key. Delay node is queued with TiScheduleDelay: due = now(EngineConfig+0x718, game clock ms) + timeoutMs + jitter, jitter = rand()*J/32768 where J = (timeoutMs<0x1000 ? ((timeoutMs+(timeoutMs<0?15:0))>>4)+1 : 0x100) taken as 16-bit, and jitter=0 if J<1 (negative timeout). Node flagged 4 with interrupt key. Wake-up value: on timeout (TiTick: due-now<1 at a frame tick) the task resumes with int 0; when interrupted the task resumes with int (due - now) = remaining ms (may be <=0 only in odd cases). All waiters with a matching key are woken, in list (FIFO) order. Waiters with the same key set by other tasks are all released by one TI_Interrupt.
x3_src: differs: random numbers come from per-task RNG channels (x3::rng, docs/arch/rng_split_r2.md), not the shared CRT rand(); same distribution, different sequence; not in bugs.md
notes: Resume goes through the group completion callback (group record +4 = NativeCompletion) with the task id as argument. TiTick 0x004b0e00 runs once per main-loop iteration. TiScheduleDelayFlagged 0x004b0bd0, TiSignalInterrupt 0x004b0bf0. On node allocation failure the callback is called at once with (param,0).

name: TI_WaitRandomForInterrupt
summary: Like TI_WaitForInterrupt with a random extra timeout.
semantics: Like TI_WaitForInterrupt with timeout = baseMs + (randMs>0 ? RandScaled(randMs) : 0) (rand()*randMs/32768, 0..randMs-1), key=args[2].value. Then TiScheduleDelay adds its own extra jitter exactly as for TI_WaitForInterrupt. Resumes with int 0 on timeout, or the remaining ms when released by TI_Interrupt(key).
x3_src: differs: random numbers come from per-task RNG channels (x3::rng, docs/arch/rng_split_r2.md), not the shared CRT rand(); same distribution, different sequence; not in bugs.md
notes: See TI_WaitForInterrupt for scheduling details. Order of rand() calls: first the randMs roll, then the jitter roll inside TiScheduleDelay (only when jitter range>=1).

name: TI_Interrupt
summary: Wakes every task waiting in TI_WaitForInterrupt with the same key; the caller continues.
semantics: TiSignalInterrupt(key): walks the delayed-timer list; every node flagged 'waiting for interrupt' (created by TI_WaitForInterrupt / TI_WaitRandomForInterrupt) whose key == arg1 is completed NOW: its task is resumed with int value = remaining time (due - clock, ms, may be <=0), and the node is removed. Tasks in plain TI_Delay are not affected. Then the caller itself continues with int 0 (not suspended). Wakeups run through the group completion callback (ResumeTask: the woken tasks are put at the head of the runnable list). Sync.
notes: TI_WaitForInterrupt(delay,key) wakes with 0 on timeout and with remaining ms on interrupt.

name: TI_GetLastFrameDelay
summary: Returns the game-clock step of the last frame in ms.
semantics: Returns EngineConfig.gameStepMs: set every frame by the frame clock (AP 0x004ee1e0) to (game clock now - game clock of the previous frame), clamped: a step outside 1..32767 ms counts as 1. It is time-warped (game ms), and 0 right after TI_SetAbsTime until the next frame. Sync. Script::TiDispatch AP 0x004b1300, FL 0x004cdf50 (same case layout).

name: TI_SetTimeWarpFactor
summary: Sets the time-warp factor (16.16, 65536 = normal speed); returns 1.
semantics: Stores args[0].value unchanged into EngineConfig+0xcc (time-warp factor, 16.16 fixed point: 65536 = 1x) and returns int 1. Engine state side effect (game speed); TiTick later adapts EngineConfig+0xd0 (the effective multiplier) from the load.
notes: Entry of this case is hooked by x3-mod (seta_restore); original code: mov [cfg+0xcc],edx.

name: TI_GetTimeWarpFactor
semantics: Returns EngineConfig+0xcc (the 16.16 time-warp factor last set by TI_SetTimeWarpFactor / the game; 65536 = normal speed). Reads engine state.

name: TI_GetTimeWarpMultiplier
summary: Returns the load governor factor that the engine multiplies with the time-warp factor.
semantics: Returns EngineConfig+0xd0 (16.16; 65536 = 1.0). TiTick adapts it every frame from the number of timers due within 40 ms * timeWarpFactor: more than 1000 such timers -> factor *= 0.7 (minimum 0.3); fewer than 200 and below 1.0 -> factor *= 1.2 (capped at 1.0); a time-warp factor lower than last frame resets it to 1.0. The game clock advances by real ms * (timeWarpFactor * this factor). Read-only for scripts. Sync. Script::TiDispatch AP 0x004b1300, FL 0x004cdf50 (same case layout).

name: TI_AddTime
semantics: Returns a+b (32-bit wrapping add of args[0].value and args[1].value). No game state touched. Synchronous.
notes: Group TI dispatcher Script::TiDispatch 0x004b1300 (thunk 0x004b12d0), name table 0x00579f80 (index = (slot-0x579f80)/4).

name: TI_SetAbsTime
summary: Sets the game clock (TI_GetAbsTime) to an absolute value.
semantics: EngineConfig.gameStepMs = 0 and gameTime = arg1 raw dword; returns arg1. Pending TI_Delay/TI_WaitForInterrupt nodes keep their absolute due times: moving the clock forward makes them fire at the next tick, moving it back delays them. The next frame step (now - previous frame time) is out of range after a big jump and counts as 1 ms. Used by savegame load/new game set-up scripts. Sync. Script::TiDispatch AP 0x004b1300, FL 0x004cdf50 (same case layout).

name: TI_GetRealTime
summary: Returns the real (wall, not time-warped) clock in milliseconds.
semantics: Result = EngineConfig+0x720 (real, un-warped elapsed time in ms-units; the counterpart of TI_GetAbsTime). Sync.
notes: Unit/epoch of +0x720 inferred only from the name; field not traced to its writer.

name: TI_ReadSystemClock
summary: Advances the clocks now and returns the real (wall) clock in ms; not a pure read.
semantics: Calls Main::TickGameClock (AP 0x004d1df0) and returns its result = EngineConfig.wallTime (the TI_GetRealTime clock) after the update. Side effects: busy-waits (QueryPerformanceCounter loop) until at least 1 ms of real time has passed since the last clock tick, adds the elapsed real ms to wallTime, and advances the game clock by the elapsed ms (clamped 1..200) times timeWarpFactor*governor (or by a pending forced step) - outside the frame step, so the next TI_GetLastFrameDelay includes it. Sync. Script::TiDispatch AP 0x004b1300, FL 0x004cdf50 (same case layout).
bugs: Design oddity (AP 0x004b159d -> 0x004d1df0, FL same; x3_src reproduces): a "read" native advances both clocks and can spin up to 1 ms; frequent calls make game time run ahead of the frame step. Not in bugs.md.
